reference.source: Nelson Textbook of Pediatrics / Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine
clinicalPearls: Caused by deficiency of biotinidase, the enzyme that recycles biotin from biocytin and liberates dietary protein-bound biotin, leading to functional biotin deficiency
Typical untreated features include seizures, hypotonia, developmental delay, ataxia, alopecia and a scaly periorificial skin rash
Sensorineural hearing loss and optic atrophy are important complications that may not fully reverse once established
Recurrent or persistent Candida infection and conjunctivitis can occur due to associated immune dysfunction
Metabolic testing may show lactic acidosis, ketosis, mild hyperammonaemia and a characteristic organic aciduria reflecting impaired carboxylase activity
This is one of the most rewarding inborn errors to treat because oral biotin supplementation reverses or prevents most manifestations
Profound deficiency (very low enzyme activity) causes more severe disease than partial deficiency, but both are treated with biotin
Included in newborn screening (enzyme activity assay), allowing pre-symptomatic treatment and excellent outcomes
reference.pathophysiology: Biotin is the cofactor for several carboxylase enzymes involved in gluconeogenesis, fatty acid synthesis and amino acid catabolism. Biotinidase cleaves biocytin to release free biotin, recycling it, and also frees biotin bound to dietary protein. When biotinidase is deficient, biotin is progressively lost and cannot be adequately reused, producing a functional deficiency that impairs the biotin-dependent carboxylases (pyruvate carboxylase, propionyl-CoA carboxylase, 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase and acetyl-CoA carboxylase). The resulting metabolic block causes lactic acidosis and abnormal organic acid accumulation, while the neurological, cutaneous, ophthalmological and auditory features reflect tissue biotin deficiency. Supplemental free biotin bypasses the recycling defect.
additionalDifferentials: Holocarboxylase synthetase deficiency (neonatal multiple carboxylase deficiency)
Mitochondrial and other causes of lactic acidosis
Acrodermatitis enteropathica (zinc deficiency) for the skin and hair findings
additionalInvestigations: Blood gas, lactate and ammonia during symptomatic episodes
Urine organic acids for the characteristic carboxylase-deficiency pattern
Molecular testing of the BTD gene to define profound versus partial deficiency
redFlags: Metabolic decompensation with lactic acidosis, ketosis and encephalopathy in an untreated infant
Intractable or unexplained seizures responsive to biotin
Progressive sensorineural hearing loss or optic atrophy, which may be irreversible if treatment is delayed
Stridor, apnoea or respiratory compromise during acute decompensation
reference.prognosis: Prognosis is excellent when biotin supplementation is started early, and screen-detected infants treated before symptoms usually develop normally; however, hearing loss, optic atrophy and neurological damage that occur before diagnosis may not fully reverse, underscoring the value of early detection.
pitfalls: Failing to consider a treatable cause in an infant with seizures, hypotonia and skin or hair changes
Stopping biotin therapy, since it must be continued lifelong
Confusing biotinidase deficiency with the neonatal-onset holocarboxylase synthetase deficiency
Assuming hearing and visual deficits will resolve, when late-treated damage may be permanent
management: Lifelong oral free biotin supplementation, which bypasses the recycling defect and reverses or prevents most manifestations
Start treatment as early as possible, ideally on newborn-screening detection before symptoms develop
Supportive management of established deficits, including hearing aids for sensorineural hearing loss and support for optic atrophy and neurological impairment
Correct lactic acidosis and metabolic decompensation during intercurrent illness
Surveillance with periodic audiological, ophthalmological and developmental assessment
Refer to metabolic medicine and provide genetic counselling with BTD testing and family screening
